messages:
Maya Chen: FYI customer AcmeRetail opened a ticket — indexing job failing with a dim mismatch after a schema migration. They say embeddings suddenly started returning 1536 dims while the vector DB expects 1024. logs below and they can reproduce. Escalating to eng. @eng-ml @eng-platform :sadpanda:

Customer - AcmeRetail: here are the logs we see on our indexer nodes:

```
Error: Embedding length mismatch: received 1536, expected 1024
  at indexer/ingest/vec_store.go:142
  at embedding/client.go:58 (embedding response: {"model":"open-embed-1536","vector_len":1536})
```

Maya Chen: they also included the curl they used to call our embeddings endpoint:

```
curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["product description sample"]}'
```

Josiah Patel: thanks. initial hunch: config drift — indexer schema pinned to 1024 dims but default model for the embed API got bumped to a 1536-dim model in a recent rollout. can you confirm which model they expect? is the DB schema mutable?

Customer - AcmeRetail: our vector DB schema is locked to 1024 because we optimized storage + search params. we didn't change anything on our side. embedding requests used to return 1024. This started yesterday after a Redwood update, per our timeline.

IndexerBot: Note: embed-service config changed in commit 8f3a2c -> default model switched to "open-embed-1536" on 2026-01-12. See: https://git.redwood/embeds/commit/8f3a2c (internal link).

Anita Gómez: ok two tracks: (1) immediate customer workaround — force embeddings to model=open-embed-1024 in their requests or pin via SDK; (2) long-term — decide whether to migrate vector DB schema to 1536 or re-embed/backfill. both have cost/latency tradeoffs.

Maya Chen: customer tried forcing model=open-embed-1024 and the indexer accepted those vectors. they reported success for a small sample. they want a backfill plan and guidance on batching to avoid rate limits and cost spikes.

Evan Liu: for backfill we should recommend a controlled rollout. suggested steps:
- pause live ingest to the indexer or route new docs to a holding queue
- spawn backfill workers that call embeddings with concurrency=8 and batch_size=64
- respect rate limits (we cap at 1200 rps for that org)
- exponential backoff on 429s and 5xx

Evan Liu: example indexer config snippet to lower concurrency and explicit model pinned:

```
indexer:
  concurrency: 8
  batch_size: 64
  embed_request:
    model: "open-embed-1024"
    retry_policy:
      max_retries: 5
      backoff_ms: 500
```

Josiah Patel: also note that batching changes can alter per-request token distribution and latency. recommend running a pre-backfill job on a small subset and validate vector lengths + search recall before full backfill.

Maya Chen: customer asked for a backfill script they can run in their k8s cluster. Anita, can you share a safe script we can give them?

Anita Gómez: posting a minimal, safe backfill script — parallelized, rate-limited, idempotent. must be run from a node with network access and billing approved.

```
#!/bin/bash
ORGANIZATION="acme"
CONCURRENCY=8
BATCH_SIZE=64
API_KEY="$REDWOOD_KEY"
PAYLOAD_FILE="batch.json"

process_batch() {
  jq -c '.[]' "$1" | xargs -n1 -P$CONCURRENCY -I{} bash -c "echo '{}' | jq -s . | \
    curl -s -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- | \
    jq -r '.data[0].embedding | @base64' > /tmp/emb_out || echo 'ERROR'"
}

# iterate over batches safely
for file in batches/*.json; do
  process_batch "$file"
  sleep 0.5 # throttle to avoid bursts
done
```

Anita Gómez: script is intentionally opinionated; we should not hand over without a short call. also warn on billing: backfill of ~10M docs at 64 per batch could cost ~X (estimate), so requires finance sign-off.

SRE Bot: Reminder — when running backfills, please tag requests with header 'X-Request-Tag: backfill/acme/2026-02-XX' so we can filter and apply temporary quota increases if needed.

Evan Liu: one more ops note — if they can't pause live ingest, we can run a streaming re-embed job that consumes from their holding queue and writes back to DB using upsert, but that needs careful idempotency keys.

Josiah Patel: long term fix: we should add a validation check at the indexer side to reject embedding dim mismatch earlier with a clearer message and autodetect model changes in our telemetry to alert us when default model changes. filing a follow-up ticket to product.

Maya Chen: customer accepted plan: pin model to open-embed-1024 for live, run a staged backfill this weekend (off-peak), will provide billing approval. they asked if Redwood can assist with running the backfill.

Anita Gómez: ops can offer 2-4 hours of hands-on help under support SLA; I can join the runbook call.

Maya Chen: assigning internal POCs: @Josiah (embeds), @Evan (sre/ops), @Anita (platform support). I'll send a calendar invite for prep tomorrow.

Customer - AcmeRetail: thanks all. please confirm cutoff window and expected downtime (they prefer none).

Maya Chen: we'll aim for zero downtime by routing writes to holding queue during the backfill window. will confirm detailed runbook in the invite. closing loop once backfill completes. :thumbsup:
